title: Manipulative design in apps for children aged 3–5
statement:
In an analysis of apps played by 160 children aged 3–5, about 80% contained at least one manipulative design feature (parasocial relationship pressure, fabricated time pressure, navigation constraints, attractive lures, or ad-based pressure), and children from lower socioeconomic households played apps with more of them, so child-facing products that avoid these patterns are a real and communicable differentiator.

Options:
- No artificial time pressure: No fabricated urgency: no fake countdowns, 'come back tomorrow' pressure or expiring rewards aimed at the child (fits: trustworthy, calm, family friendly)
- No character pressure: Characters never nag or guilt an idle child; no parasocial pressure prompts (fits: gentle, nurturing, respectful)
- Parent-only commerce: Purchases and ads confined to a parent-only area, never pitched by a character inside the child's flow (fits: trustworthy, safe, transparent)
- Free navigation: Always-visible, child-reachable back and exit controls (no navigation traps) (fits: respectful, simple, friendly)
- Plain promise to parents: Landing-page statement to parents on whether the product has ads or in-app purchases, with the page design matching that promise (fits: transparent, trustworthy, family friendly)
appliesWhen: Applies to: kids apps, kids games, family subscription products, educational products. Audience: children under 10, parents.

source.title: Prevalence and Characteristics of Manipulative Design in Mobile Applications Used by Children
source.authors: Jenny Radesky; Alexis Hiniker; Caroline McLaren; Eliz Akgun; Alexandria Schaller; Heidi M. Weeks; Scott Campbell; Ashley N. Gearhardt
